sendTest: Someone pointed a Chinese AI at a database and it found 19 unknown ways to break in. Ninety minutes. Seven emergency fixes went out.
centralClaim: A researcher used the Chinese AI model Kimi K3 to find 19 previously unknown vulnerabilities in the Redis database in about 90 minutes.

corroboration.quote: Chaofan Shou said on X that Kimi K3 agents found 19 Redis zero-days in about 90 minutes, and said another run produced the Redis 8.8.0 exploit in 27 minutes.

The user “Chaofan Shou” posted on X that he found a total of 19 zero-day vulnerabilities in the then-current version 8.8.0 of the redis database in 90 minutes using the AI from the Chinese start-up Moonshot AI.

caption:
A researcher pointed a Chinese AI at Redis, and it found 19 unknown ways in. It took 90 minutes.

Redis is an open source database that keeps data in memory so software can reach it fast. On July 23 the project shipped seven security releases, right after working attack code for the flaws was published. Anyone running an affected version has to update.

The AI was Kimi K3, from the Chinese company Moonshot. Demand for it has run so far ahead of the computers behind it that Moonshot has temporarily stopped taking new subscriptions.

The caveat matters. The count of 19, the 90 minutes, and how much of the work the AI did on its own are all things the researcher reported. Redis confirms the flaws and the fixes. It does not confirm the count.

So does a machine that finds 19 holes before lunch make software safer, or does it just make the race faster?

Sources: thehackernews.com, heise.de

AI-assisted.

#AI #cybersecurity #Redis #KimiK3

captionEvidence.quote: Chaofan Shou said on X that Kimi K3 agents found 19 Redis zero-days in about 90 minutes, and said another run produced the Redis 8.8.0 exploit in 27 minutes. Those counts, timings, and the claimed degree of autonomy remain self-reported. Redis's public record confirms the flaws and fixes. It does not validate the claimed zero-day count or how independently the agents worked.
Redis shipped seven security releases on July 23 after researchers published authenticated RCE PoCs for stock Redis 6.2.22, 7.4.9, 8.6.4, and 8.8.0.
The developers of the open-source in-memory database redis have released updated versions that close several vulnerabilities within it.
The Kimi-K3 AI from Moonshot AI is experiencing high demand. The provider has temporarily stopped new subscriptions due to GPU bottlenecks.
